note: How acolyte sculpts are arranged on a duty tile. Read by tools/ui_debug/generate_duty_board_check.py, generate_placement_sheet.py and generate_duty_sow.py. Edit the numbers here rather than in a page.
one_set_on_purpose: These are absolute distances in real device pixels and they are used at EVERY sculpt size, not scaled per size. 210 is the working size, so 210 is what they are tuned against. The consequence, stated rather than discovered: at 90 px the same numbers leave the figures standing well apart, because a spread of 110 is wider than a 90 px figure is tall. That is expected, not a fault - the smaller sizes are there to glance at, not to tune against.
sizes_note: Which sculpt sizes the sow page offers a button for. The placement sheet ignores this and shows every size the tray has rendered, because comparing them is what it is for; the sow page is played at one size and asks which. NOT a per-size table of numbers -- there is still one spread, one set-back and one rank gap, used whatever is on screen. Name another size here and its button appears; the tray has to have rendered it first (tools/ui_debug/make_tray_figures.py).
spread_note: Distance between neighbouring sculpts in a rank, centre to centre. The sculpts are not one width: measured at 210 px tall, three of the four are 91 px across and the fourth is 108, so any spread means two different things depending on who is standing there. At 110 the three narrow figures stand about a fifth of a width apart and the wide one just touches its neighbour -- 110 is roughly where overlap stops for every seat rather than for most of them.
back_note: How far the middle of three is set back from the other two. A flat row of three identical silhouettes is the hardest case to read, and lifting the centre one breaks the repeat.
rank_note: How far a back rank stands behind the front one, used at four and five sculpts.
order_note: grouped keeps a seat's sculpts adjacent and countable; arrival never reorders what is already down. Measured, the two move the same number of sculpts per drop (2.73 of them), because the shuffle comes from the formation changing shape with the count, not from the ordering.
mark_note: floor, foot, box or gild. A footprint promises a SPOT, which a rule that re-lays the whole group cannot keep; the floor claims only the tile, so the arrangement is free to follow its own rules.
depth_note: haze blends toward the tile colour and is ground-dependent; dark goes toward black and is not. full_at is the depth in real px at which the cue reaches about 63% of `amount` -- the cue is 1-exp(-y/full_at), so it is absolute and monotonic: a figure never becomes clearer because another moved further away, and a third rank still reads as deeper than a second.
